occurrenceRemarks: The photo is by ichthyologist Dr Mark V Erdmann, identified by him and posted here with his permission. I posted this because most of the iNat photos of this species, including the taxon photos, were incorrect at the time of posting in that they did not show the prolonged 3rd dorsal spine characteristic of the true Bluedot Goby, Asterropteryx ensifera. That has now been corrected. Unfortunately, many photos on Fishbase are still incorrect, even though Fishbase clearly states "prolonged third dorsal spine, forms long filament in adult." Even worse, the popular field guide, *Reef Fish Identification, Tropical Pacific*, also has an incorrect photo! IMHO, photos purporting to be A ensifera and lacking a prolonged 3rd dorsal spine are most likely the dark form of Asterropteryx striata. Please see photos 2-4, supporting my claim. Photo 2 is from the Allen & Erdmann app Reef Fishes of the East Indies; photo 3 is from Dr. John E Randall's book Reef and Shore Fishes of the South Pacific; photo 4 is from Coastal Fishes of the Western Indian Ocean volume 5.
